original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,3,3), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every three points determine three distinct distances, equivalently a set with no isosceles triangles, including degenerate collinear ones.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 28 in the current arXiv v3 HTML version (the same question appears as Section 6, Problem 27 on p. 12 of the June 7, 2014 PDF): find the asymptotic value of φ(n,3,3). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s intended target: it asks for the asymptotic value of φ(n,3,3), keeps the planar setting, and correctly uses the equivalent reformulation that forbids isosceles triangles, including degenerate collinear ones. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: State explicitly that the point set is a set P ⊂ R^2 of n distinct points, and that distances are ordinary Euclidean distances. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Define D(P) (or spell it out) as the number of distinct distances determined by unordered pairs of points of P; the paper’s notation φ(n,3,3) is a minimum of this quantity over admissible sets. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Make explicit that the local condition means every 3-point subset of P determines at least 3 distinct pairwise distances, i.e. all three pairwise distances are different. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
State that the asymptotic question is as n → ∞. This is implicit in the paper’s phrase “find the asymptotic value.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
refined_question: As n → ∞, determine the asymptotic growth of φ(n,3,3), where for a finite set P ⊂ R^2, D(P) denotes the number of distinct Euclidean distances {|pq| : p,q ∈ P, p ≠ q}, and φ(n,3,3) is the minimum of D(P) over all n-point sets P ⊂ R^2 such that every 3-point subset of P determines at least 3 distinct pairwise distances. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as n → ∞, determine the minimum possible number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P ⊂ R^2 that spans no isosceles triangles, where degenerate collinear isosceles triples are also forbidden. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
justification: The paper first defines φ(n,k,l) for planar n-point sets with the local property that every k points determine at least l distinct distances, and then specializes to φ(n,3,3). In the immediately adjacent discussion, it explicitly identifies φ(n,3,3) with the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set with no isosceles triangles, adding that degenerate collinear isosceles triangles are included. The official open problem attached to this discussion is “Find the asymptotic value of φ(n,3,3),” while Erdős’s nearby remark that φ(n,3,3)=ω(n) is presented as a conjectural comment, not as the named open problem itself. So your draft is targeting the right problem; it mainly needed the notation to be unpacked so the question is fully stand-alone. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
